In 5–15% of cases of diverticulitis, fistulous pathways appear after the acute process has resolved. The most common such pathway is a colovesical fistula, which manifests as thickening of the bladder adjacent to thickening of the colonic loop, together with air within the bladder(3,4), as depicted in Figure 6.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Sagittal contrast-enhanced CT panel shows a loculated abdominal wall collection marked by a red arrow, presented as a rare extra-abdominal complication of acute diverticulitis; the case CT also demonstrated colonic diverticula. B: Axial contrast-enhanced CT panel shows a left anterior abdominal wall abscess extending through the muscular layers, marked by a red arrow, in a case report of acute diverticulitis with this rare complication. C: Axial contrast-enhanced CT panel shows a well-demarcated heterogeneous abdominal wall abscess marked by a red arrow, abutting adjacent bowel, in a case report of acute diverticulitis complicated by extra-abdominal abscess.

panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced CT images showing abdominal wall abscess. (A) Sagittal view reveals a loculated hypodense collection involving the left anterior abdominal wall (red arrow). (B-C) Axial sections demonstrate the abscess extending through the muscular layers (rectus and obliques), abutting adjacent bowel structures. The collection appears well-demarcated and heterogeneous, consistent with a mature abscess cavity (red arrows).
